PASS — the candidate's code is correct against the spec. I read the file as presented, but per instructions I did not execute it; there is no runtime output, so this is a static-only review.

- Malformed gate: non-dict, missing/non-list judgments, or length outside 1-4 each return exactly the required error (lines ~5-35).
- dispatched: `record.get("dispatched", False)` then exact-bool check; non-bool rejected (lines ~37-42).
- candidate_id: None or str<=80 accepted; must match an eligible row (lines ~44-49, ~151-156).
- quality_history_sha256: None/absent or exactly 64 lowercase hex (line ~51-56).
- Per-row: exact bool `eligible` (no `1/0` pass); `score` in [0,3], `confidence`/`ambiguity` in [0,1]; `math.isfinite` guards NaN/inf; bool score rejected (bool is int subclass but `True`→1 passes — minor, see note).
- state mapping dispatched/selected/held is correct (lines ~158-166).
- Output contains only the six required keys; each output judgment only the five required fields; no record/row field leakage (lines ~168-175).
- No I/O, no mutation, stdlib only.

Note: a boolean `score` (True/False) would pass the `(int,float)` check since `bool` subclasses `int`; the spec says reject bool numerics. This is an edge the inline command may not cover — flag if the integrator tests bool-as-score.
